title: WP - 2026-11-04 - Simon Beyeler: Forecasting the post-COVID inflation surge in Switzerland
summary: The surge in inflation after the COVID-19 pandemic caught forecasters and policy makers by surprise: shocks treated as transitory turned out to be persistent, producing large forecast errors. Watson (2026) asks whether the U.S. surge could instead have been recognised as persistent in real time using Unobserved-Components Stochastic Volatility (UC-SV) models. This paper replicates and extends that exercise for Switzerland, using (i) total Swiss CPI inflation and (ii) sectoral inflation for 22 expenditure groups - both extended with an explicit seasonal component since the Swiss CPI is not seasonally adjusted. Both models attribute the bulk of the 2021-2023 Swiss surge to the permanent trend rather than to transitory noise and reach that reading from data available in real time. In the sectoral model, the sector-specific trends account for most of the variance, whereas the common inflation trend plays only a minor role.

summary: The National Center of Excellence for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Safety (National LNG Center) will host a series of informational workshops on best practices for LNG safety titled, "LNG Safety Best Practices Workshop." The workshops are free; will be hosted in-person with select hybrid sessions offered virtually; and will require advance registration. Each workshop will be a full day and will cover a variety of best practices each session. PHMSA established the National LNG Center in 2023 pursuant to section 111 of the Protecting Our Infrastructure of Pipelines and Enhancing Safety (PIPES) Act of 2020 (Pub. Consistent with this mandate, the workshop series will bring together representatives from industry, government, academia, emergency response organizations, and other stakeholders to promote information sharing and continuous improvement in LNG safety.

title: Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products; Guidance for Industry; Availability
issuer: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance titled "Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products." The guidance document provides recommendations to help assure the potency of human cellular therapy or gene therapy (CGT) products at all stages of the product lifecycle. FDA is recommending a comprehensive approach to potency assurance of CGT products that is grounded in quality risk management. For investigational products, we describe how to progressively implement a strategy for potency assurance during product development and provide additional considerations to help assure the potency of products that are undergoing rapid clinical development. For licensed products, we describe requirements for potency assurance, including testing required for lot release assays. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance of the same title issued on December 28, 2023.
